title: Standard hand signals (Appendix A to Subpart CC of 29 CFR 1926)

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A
source.license: Public domain. Work of the United States Government (17 U.S.C. 105).

notes.quote: Standard Method means the protocol in appendix A of this subpart for hand signals.

When using hand signals, the Standard Method must be used (see appendix A of this subpart). Exception: Where use of the Standard Method for hand signals is infeasible, or where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in the Standard Method, non-standard hand signals may be used in accordance with paragraph (c)(2) of this section.

When using non-standard hand signals, the signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one) must contact each other prior to the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals that will be used.
Anyone who becomes aware of a safety problem must alert the operator or signal person by giving the stop or emergency stop signal.
The operator must obey a stop (or emergency stop) signal, irrespective of who gives it.
Hand signal charts must be either posted on the equipment or conspicuously posted in the vicinity of the hoisting operations.
If hand signals are used, the signal person must know and understand the Standard Method for hand signals.

signals.name: STOP
signals.description: With arm extended horizontally to the side, palm down, arm is swung back and forth.
signals.caption: STOP – With arm extended horizontally to the side, palm down, arm is swung back and forth.

teaching_tip.text: One arm out flat, palm down, sweeping side to side, means stop the motion now.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: EMERGENCY STOP
signals.description: With both arms extended horizontally to the side, palms down, arms are swung back and forth.
signals.caption: EMERGENCY STOP – With both arms extended horizontally to the side, palms down, arms are swung back and forth.

teaching_tip.text: It is STOP done with both arms at once; two arms means emergency.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: HOIST
signals.description: With upper arm extended to the side, forearm and index finger pointing straight up, hand and finger make small circles.
signals.caption: HOIST – With upper arm extended to the side, forearm and index finger pointing straight up, hand and finger make small circles.

teaching_tip.text: The finger points up and circles, as if winding the load line up.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: RAISE BOOM
signals.description: With arm extended horizontally to the side, thumb points up with other fingers closed.
signals.caption: RAISE BOOM – With arm extended horizontally to the side, thumb points up with other fingers closed.

teaching_tip.text: A thumb is the boom; thumb up on a straight arm raises it.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: SWING
signals.description: With arm extended horizontally, index finger points in direction that boom is to swing.
signals.caption: SWING – With arm extended horizontally, index finger points in direction that boom is to swing.

teaching_tip.text: Point where the boom should go; the pointing finger, not the thumb, means swing.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: RETRACT TELESCOPING BOOM
signals.description: With hands to the front at waist level, thumbs point at each other with other fingers closed.
signals.caption: RETRACT TELESCOPING BOOM – With hands to the front at waist level, thumbs point at each other with other fingers closed.

teaching_tip.text: Thumbs pointing toward each other pull the boom sections in.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: RAISE THE BOOM AND LOWER THE LOAD
signals.description: With arm extended horizontally to the side and thumb pointing up, fingers open and close while load movement is desired.
signals.caption: RAISE THE BOOM AND LOWER THE LOAD – With arm extended horizontally to the side and thumb pointing up, fingers open and close while load movement is desired.

teaching_tip.text: Start from RAISE BOOM (thumb up), then flex the fingers for as long as the load should move.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: DOG EVERYTHING
signals.description: Hands held together at waist level.
signals.caption: DOG EVERYTHING – Hands held together at waist level.

teaching_tip.text: Hands together at the waist means hold everything; no motion until the next signal.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: LOWER
signals.description: With arm and index finger pointing down, hand and finger make small circles.
signals.caption: LOWER – With arm and index finger pointing down, hand and finger make small circles.

teaching_tip.text: The mirror of HOIST; the finger points down and circles.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: LOWER BOOM
signals.description: With arm extended horizontally to the side, thumb points down with other fingers closed.
signals.caption: LOWER BOOM – With arm extended horizontally to the side, thumb points down with other fingers closed.

teaching_tip.text: The mirror of RAISE BOOM; thumb down on a straight arm lowers the boom.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: EXTEND TELESCOPING BOOM
signals.description: With hands to the front at waist level, thumbs point outward with other fingers closed.
signals.caption: EXTEND TELESCOPING BOOM – With hands to the front at waist level, thumbs point outward with other fingers closed.

teaching_tip.text: Thumbs pointing away from each other push the boom sections out.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: TRAVEL/TOWER TRAVEL
signals.description: With all fingers pointing up, arm is extended horizontally out and back to make a pushing motion in the direction of travel.
signals.caption: TRAVEL/TOWER TRAVEL – With all fingers pointing up, arm is extended horizontally out and back to make a pushing motion in the direction of travel.

teaching_tip.text: An open hand pushes the air the way the machine should travel.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: LOWER THE BOOM AND RAISE THE LOAD
signals.description: With arm extended horizontally to the side and thumb pointing down, fingers open and close while load movement is desired.
signals.caption: LOWER THE BOOM AND RAISE THE LOAD – With arm extended horizontally to the side and thumb pointing down, fingers open and close while load movement is desired.

teaching_tip.text: Start from LOWER BOOM (thumb down), then flex the fingers for as long as the load should move.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: MOVE SLOWLY
signals.description: A hand is placed in front of the hand that is giving the action signal.
signals.caption: MOVE SLOWLY – A hand is placed in front of the hand that is giving the action signal.

teaching_tip.text: Not a motion on its own; the second hand in front slows whatever the signaling hand calls for.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: USE AUXILIARY HOIST (whipline)
signals.description: With arm bent at elbow and forearm vertical, elbow is tapped with other hand. Then regular signal is used to indicate desired action.
signals.caption: USE AUXILIARY HOIST (whipline) – With arm bent at elbow and forearm vertical, elbow is tapped with other hand. Then regular signal is used to indicate desired action.

teaching_tip.text: Tap the elbow to pick the whipline, then give the motion signal.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: CRAWLER CRANE TRAVEL, BOTH TRACKS
signals.description: Rotate fists around each other in front of body; direction of rotation away from body indicates travel forward; rotation towards body indicates travel backward.
signals.caption: CRAWLER CRANE TRAVEL, BOTH TRACKS – Rotate fists around each other in front of body; direction of rotation away from body indicates travel forward; rotation towards body indicates travel backward.

teaching_tip.text: Fists roll like the tracks; rolling away from the body is forward, toward the body is backward.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: USE MAIN HOIST
signals.description: A hand taps on top of the head. Then regular signal is given to indicate desired action.
signals.caption: USE MAIN HOIST – A hand taps on top of the head. Then regular signal is given to indicate desired action.

teaching_tip.text: Tap the head to pick the main hoist, then give the motion signal.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: CRAWLER CRANE TRAVEL, ONE TRACK
signals.description: Indicate track to be locked by raising fist on that side. Rotate other fist in front of body in direction that other track is to travel.
signals.caption: CRAWLER CRANE TRAVEL, ONE TRACK – Indicate track to be locked by raising fist on that side. Rotate other fist in front of body in direction that other track is to travel.

teaching_tip.text: The raised fist marks the track that stays locked; the rolling fist drives the other one.

source.edition: 29 CFR Ch. XVII (7-1-25 Edition), Part 1926, Subpart CC, Appendix A

signals.name: TROLLEY TRAVEL
signals.description: With palm up, fingers closed and thumb pointing in direction of motion, hand is jerked horizontally in direction trolley is to travel.
signals.caption: TROLLEY TRAVEL – With palm up, fingers closed and thumb pointing in direction of motion, hand is jerked horizontally in direction trolley is to travel.

teaching_tip.text: Palm up, thumb leading, short jerks toward where the trolley should run.
